annotations.text: Though he broke both legs in descending at Domodossola, M. Chavez is quite happy, for, in flying over the Alps from Switzerland to Italy, he has accomplished a feat that will live for years in the annals of airmanship. He is, however, unable to explain how he came to fall after having surmounted greater difficulties and the earth was so

near. He remarked smilingly yesterday: "In spite of all, I am happy to have flown the Alps, accomplishing a feat which was believed to be impossible." The photograph shows the start of the flight at Brigue, and was taken a few moments before the airman disappeared over the mountains.-(Daily Mirror photograph.)

Loch, Irish Lough, and

Several holiday fatalities occurred yesterday. As two Leven anglers named Mohir and Murray were changing seats in their boat on Loch Lomond in the dark early yesterday morning, Missouri, aged sixty, fell overboard. Murray dived to his rescue, but could not find him, and his body was recovered later.

A sailing-boat containing four people capsized while returning from Portaferry to Killyleagh, in Strangford Lough, Co. Down, last night. One man named John Morrow was drowned, and Alexander Wilson died after being rescued.
While on holiday in Devon, Robert Nicholls, of Padding, hired a boat on the River Dart at Stoke, and later he was found drowned. Accidental death was the verdict at the inquest yesterday.
ONIONS AS ANTIDOTE.

All workmen should be encouraged to make use of onions and garlic in their diet, and no wines, spirits or beer or alcoholic liquor should be taken into a white lead factory, advises Dr. K. W. Goadby, in the report, just issued, of the Home Office Departmental Committee on Lead Poisoning.
BEAUTY SHOW RESULTS.

After keen voting at Folkestone last night the beauty competition resulted as follows: Miss Kitty Darlin (Plymouth), 1; Miss Mamie Whittaker, the English beauty queen (London), 2; Mme. Simone de Beryl (Paris), 3.

GRATEFUL MALAY GUIDES.
Bisley Team Thanks British Public Who Made Them "Feel at Home."
Subadar Fatch Singh, Adjutant of the Malay States Guides' team lately at Bisley, has sent a grateful message to this country from the team for the "two happy months they spent in England."

After particularly thanking the president of the council of the N.R.A. for the treatment they "have received at their hands at all reasonable and unreasonable times," the subadar says the team "carry back with them the greatest esteem for the British public, who have made them feel at home wherever they had occasion to go during their visit."
SHOT FROM A TRAIN.

As a crowded special train on the Great Northern of Ireland line was leaving Londerry last night, after the celebration of the anniversary of the relief of Londerry, a revolver was fired from a carriage window, and Frederick McDonagh, standing at his father's door, was struck in the arm.
